minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved the dump-removal and 7-11 Mass Ave subdivision notices, plus a Laurel Lane compliance certificate.
minutes.summary: The commission, meeting by Zoom, closed hearings on a municipal dump-site removal and an eight-unit subdivision on Massachusetts Avenue, issued a certificate of compliance, and continued two other hearings. It also discussed whether to take a position on tax-lien properties, the trails grant and a property maintenance scope of work.

budget_items.topic: Economic alternatives analysis, 711 Mass Ave subdivision
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant's representative presented a cost analysis comparing eight units with six, saying six units would yield roughly zero profit and eight yield a thin margin, driven by material costs.
A quote from an auto body shop to move the new trail gates to the DPW yard; the commission authorized spending up to the quoted amount from the timber rights fund.

The open space committee recommended not selling tax liens on several parcels; the commission wanted the taxes owed, likely auction value and demolition cost of the lake lodge before taking a position.
Gates and trail map signs funded through the trails grant are being fabricated and installed; sign graphics were redone at higher resolution.

decisions.decision: Tax lien position tabled; chair to send questions on demolition cost, likely auction price and taxes owed to the tax collector and staff.
Chair asked staff to go back to the DPW contact for a recommendation of someone to develop the scope of work for the maintenance property.
A workshop on bylaws to be scheduled.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted, on a roll call with all members aye, to approve the notice of intent to remove an old dump site on conservation land at Fairview Road.
It approved the notice of intent for the subdivision at 711 Massachusetts Avenue after the applicant's representative presented an economic alternatives analysis.
The commission tabled a position on tax-lien properties and will send questions on demolition cost, likely auction value and taxes owed to the tax collector and staff.
It continued the Townsend Harbor Road and Chase Road hearings, and approved a small timber rights fund purchase order to move the new trail gates.
The commission approved a certificate of compliance for 30 Laurel Lane, and scheduled a bylaws workshop with no date set.

why_it_matters: The dump-site removal on town conservation land and the tax-lien question on open-space parcels both bear on what the town spends on land it owns or might take back.
The subdivision approval and the two continued hearings decide how much new building is allowed near wetlands in town, and the timber rights fund and trails grant pay for trail work.
watch_next: The Townsend Harbor Road hearing returns on March 2nd and the Chase Road hearing in March.
The tax collector's answers on the tax-lien properties, and a date for the bylaws workshop.
